 Seoul Sees First Snow 12 Days Earlier Than Average Amid Early Cold Snap
 SBS World News 
 Seoul 
 Published 
 2026.11.08 21:09 
 View 
 View Count 
 PIP 닫기 
 Strong cold air continuing to flow in from the northwest has brought an early cold snap. 
 Amid this cold weather, Seoul saw news of its first snow today (November 8). 
 This was observed 12 days earlier than average and 26 days earlier than last year. 
 Because the intensity was not strong, the snow did not accumulate, and it turned to rain as temperatures rose during the day. 
 Rain is expected to continue mainly in the central regions until late tonight. 
 The expected precipitation is from a minimum of 5 mm to a maximum of 20 mm, while up to 5 cm of snow is expected to accumulate in the mountainous areas of Gangwon Province. 
 Tomorrow, Monday, rain is forecasted for the east coast, southern regions, and Jeju. 
 It will begin early in the morning in Jeju and South Jeolla Province, and expand to the east coast and southern regions by the afternoon. 
 The expected precipitation is from 5 mm to a maximum of 30 mm. 
 Amid the early cold, many people probably took out their winter coats. 
 The cold weather will continue for a while, and temperatures are expected to recover to seasonal averages toward the middle of the week. 
 Tomorrow morning, ice may form in some inland and mountainous areas of Gangwon Province. 
 Looking at morning temperatures, Seoul will start at 4°C (39°F) and Daegu at 6°C (43°F), while daytime temperatures will reach 13°C (55°F) in Seoul and 15°C (59°F) in Busan, resulting in a large diurnal temperature range from the morning. 
 The rain falling tomorrow will mostly stop by night, and skies will clear up again starting Tuesday. 
 (Weather Forecaster An Su-jin)
